newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev ends softer on rise in dollar demand.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev ends softer on rise in dollar demand.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed at 244-245 per dollar, down from 242-244 in early trade as dollar demand topped supply amid the central bank's absence from the market in the afternoon, dealers said.
"Final clients bid for larger foreign currency volumes, in the afternoon, pushing the lev down to 242-244," a commercial bank dealer said.
The central bank sold small dollar volumes to final clients near 243.00/50 levs in the morning but the lev was pressured to 244-245 after it withdrew from the market in the afternoon, dealers said.
Central bank officials were not available for comment.
The rise in dollar demand was probably due to clients' needs to meet pending payments rather than to a dollar rush after a interest rate cut, traders said.

The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) last night cut its main interest rate (CIR) to 15 percent per month or 180 percent annually, from 20 percent or 240 percent respecively, to go in force from November 4.

Dealers estimated pressure on the lev after the rate cut as relatively low because most financial institutions have already squared forex positions after a previous rate cut two weeks ago, traders said.
